title: Differentiation: Gradients, Tangents and Stationary Points
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Differentiation Worksheets
standard_text: Understand the derivative of f(x) as the gradient of the tangent; differentiate xⁿ; apply differentiation to find gradients, tangents and normals, maxima and minima and stationary points; identify where functions are increasing or decreasing.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on differentiation: differentiating powers of x, gradients, tangents and normals, stationary points and increasing and decreasing functions. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

Differentiate term by term: multiply by the power, then reduce the power by 1. dy/dx gives the gradient of the curve.

Tangent: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Normal gradient = −1/m. Stationary points: dy/dx = 0; d²y/dx² > 0 minimum, < 0 maximum.

Example

Gradient of y = x³ − 2x at x = 2.

dy/dx = 3x² − 2

12 − 2

Answer: 10

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to reduce the power.
  • Differentiating a constant to 1.
  • Using the tangent gradient for the normal.

faq.a: The gradient of the curve at each point, which is the rate of change of y with respect to x.

faq.q: How do you find a stationary point?
faq.a: Solve dy/dx = 0 for x, then find y. Use the second derivative to decide if it is a maximum or a minimum.

items.q: At which point does f(x) = −x³ + 3x² − 9 have a local maximum?
items.e: f′ changes from + to − at x = 2, so f has a local maximum there: x = 2.

items.q: Find the local minimum value of f(x) = 2x³ − 24x − 5.
items.e: f′(x) = 0 at −2 and 2. f″(2) > 0, so the local minimum is f(2) = −37.

items.e: P = x(30 − x); dP/dx = 30 − 2x = 0 gives x = 15, so the maximum product is 15 × 15 = 225.
